transcript.text: Bottom rack on my Beko DVN05320W isn't getting clean and I've noticed the lower spray arm has a crack along one side and wobbles. Do I just need a new arm?

Quite possibly, yes. A crack along the arm lets water escape from the split instead of the jets, so pressure drops and the arm may not spin properly. The wobble is the one thing to check first. It may just come from the cracked arm, or the hub or mounting it sits on may be worn. If the mounting is the problem, a new arm alone could still wobble. 1. Switch the dishwasher off at the wall and pull out the bottom basket. On most models the lower arm lifts straight up off its centre post or unclips. Look closely at the crack. If it's an open split, that alone is enough to explain poor cleaning.
2. While the arm is out, look at the hub in the middle of the arm and the post it sits on. If the hole in the arm's hub is worn oval or chipped, the wobble is the arm's own fault. If the post or its seating is cracked, broken or loose, that part matters too, not just the arm.
3. Rinse the jets under the tap and poke out any debris or scale with a cocktail stick. Then take out and clean the filter. Partly blocked jets or a clogged filter make poor cleaning worse, whatever the crack is doing.
4. Refit the arm, put the basket back and spin the arm by hand. It should turn freely without catching on the basket or on tall items poking through. One question tells me whether this is just the arm. Is the top rack still coming out clean? If it is, the problem is local to the lower arm and a new arm should sort it. If both racks are poor, there's probably something upstream as well, such as low water fill or weak circulation, and a new arm wouldn't be the whole answer.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

Top rack is coming out clean, it's just the bottom. I've had the arm out already - spins but wobbles, hub looks fine. A couple of the holes had limescale in them but the filters are clean. Do you know the part number for the arm?

I can't give you a reliable part number. Beko often uses different arms within the same model range depending on the production run, so a number from me could easily be wrong. 1. Find the rating label, usually on the edge of the door or the side of the door frame. Note the full model number and the product/serial number printed there.
2. Search Beko's own spares site, or a reputable UK spares supplier, using those numbers. Compare the listing photo with your old arm before buying, checking the shape, the hub and how it clips on. On the diagnosis, your findings point clearly at the arm. Only the bottom rack is poor, the top is fine and the filters are clean. That means water is reaching the machine properly, and the problem is local to the lower arm. A crack along the arm leaks pressure, so the jets that matter fire weakly. That fits well. I'd say it's fairly likely, not certain, that the arm alone is the fix. There's one gap before you spend money. 1. With the machine switched off, look at that post or seat. Wiggle it gently and look for cracks or a chipped top. If it's solid, the wobble is probably the cracked arm flexing or sitting unevenly, and a new arm should cure both the wobble and the poor cleaning. If it's loose or damaged, a new arm will still wobble on it, so that piece matters too.
2. In the meantime, clear the scaled holes properly with a cocktail stick. If scale is building up, it's worth checking the dishwasher salt is topped up and the water hardness setting suits your area. Otherwise a new arm will scale up the same way over time. If the post is solid and a new arm still leaves the bottom rack poor, let me know. The next things to look at would be how the arm is seated and how the dishes are loaded around it.
The hub and bearing look intact to me, nothing chipped or broken that I can see. Haven't wiggled it though. I'll check the rating plate for the product code and search with that.

That sounds sensible. With the hub and bearing looking intact, the top rack clean and the filters clear, the cracked lower spray arm is by far the most likely cause. I'd put it at fairly likely rather than certain. The crack lets water escape sideways, so the jets fire weakly. A split arm can also flex and sit unevenly, which would explain the wobble. The one thing still unconfirmed is whether the post the arm sits on is firm. It takes seconds and is worth doing before you order: 1. With the dishwasher switched off at the wall, lift the arm off. Hold the centre post or seat and wiggle it gently side to side.
2. If it feels solid, the wobble is down to the arm itself, and a new lower spray arm should sort out both the wobble and the cleaning.
3. If it moves or rocks, the mounting is worn too. A new arm on its own would still wobble, so that piece would need looking at as well. When you search with the product code from the rating plate, check the listing photo against your old arm, including the hub shape and how it clips on. If a sound arm still leaves the bottom rack poor, the next things to look at would be scale in the jets (keep the salt topped up and the hardness setting right) and whether anything in the load is blocking the arm.
